hypotheses_validated.claim: Verifier finding 1 (major) was real and is fixed: code outside the lock could make check_golden --run report OK while no golden test body ran
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Reproduced with the old tool on the verifier's scratch repo: tests/__init__.py patching _pytest.python.Function.runtest gave 'golden suite OK: 1 passed' for a golden test that asserts False; an unchecked-hash tests/golden/__pycache__/__init__.cpython-313.pyc gave 'golden lock OK' and 'golden suite OK'. Fix in check_golden.py: --run stages a fresh temp directory holding only the locked files (re-hashed from the bytes actually copied) plus generated empty __init__.py files, rootdir/confcutdir/cwd = that directory, child started with -E and -X pycache_prefix=<empty dir>, and only the hearth package is importable from python/ (meta-path finder; python/ is no longer on sys.path). The lock now fails on symlinks/junctions anywhere in tests/golden (lstat S_ISLNK or a Windows name-surrogate reparse tag) and on unchecked-hash .pyc files in __pycache__; the script drops its own directory from sys.path when run as __main__ (realpath compare). After the fix the same two reproductions give 'golden suite FAILED (0 passed, 1 failed ...)' rc=1 and 'BYTECODE ... golden lock BROKEN' rc=1. New tests (all fail against the gen-002 tool, all pass now): test_golden_run_ignores_code_outside_the_lock[tests/__init__.py | python/colorsys.py | hearth bytecode] (each first proves the vector fools plain pytest), test_golden_lock_rejects_unchecked_bytecode, test_golden_lock_rejects_links (junction on Windows, symlink on Linux/WSL; also tests/golden itself as a link), test_golden_stage_copies_only_locked_files (incl. tamper after check -> ManifestError), test_golden_run_uses_locked_conftest, test_golden_tool_ignores_modules_planted_beside_it. The in-process limit (hearth package and engine library run inside pytest) and the tool's own non-lockability are documented in the docstring and README; CI now runs check_golden.py from the PR base revision.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Verifier finding 2 (major) was real and is fixed: a --timeout below the test's runtime gave a 100% mutation score that passed --min-score
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Reproduced with the old tool: weak calc test scored 22.7% by default but 100% (timeout 22) with --timeout 0.05 --min-score 1.0, rc 0; --timeout -1 also 100%. Fix in mutate.py: --timeout must be a positive finite number (argparse type), the baseline runs under the same --timeout (600 s default) and exit 2 if it times out, mutant timeout = max(requested, 2 x baseline, baseline + 5 s) with a warning when raised, report fields timeout_requested_s and warnings, and a score made only of timeouts is flagged and fails --min-score. After: --timeout 0.05 -> 'did not finish within 0.05 s on the unmutated code; raise --timeout' rc 2; -1 -> argparse error rc 2; --timeout 0.5 -> raised to 5.1 s, 22.7% (same as default). Verifier's C case (hxdemo.c --lines 10,15,22,25, 16 mutants, seed 1): --timeout 0.2 -> rc 2 (baseline 0.3 s); --timeout 2 -> raised to 5.3 s, 68.8% (killed 11, survived 5), identical to the default-timeout result, rc 1 under --min-score 1.0. Tests: test_mutate_timeout_floor_and_parsing, test_mutate_short_timeout_cannot_inflate_the_score, test_mutate_score_made_only_of_timeouts_is_flagged, test_mutate_all_killed_report (all fail on the gen-002 tool).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Minor findings 3-8 were real and are fixed, each with a test that fails on the gen-002 tools
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Reproduced first: timestamp 12345 -> TypeError in is_date_time under jsonschema and a 0-byte --json output; measurements 5/true -> TypeError in both engines; old ecma_regex gave ^\s$ vs NBSP False, ^a.b$ vs CR True, ^[]a]$ vs a True, ^[^]$ re.error; adr breaker with INVARIANTS.md deleted said 'invariants unchanged' rc 0; friction counted three different unsigned failing commands as one signature and 'check --task T99-none' exited 2; validate_handover --new NOPE-task / ../escape --write created files (one outside the dir); mutate --since no-such-rev outside git mutated every line rc 0. Fixes: is_date_time ignores non-strings, measurements iterated only when a list, check_one() turns any unexpected exception into a per-file error; a real ECMA-262 'u'-flag translator (\d \w \b ASCII, \s = ECMA white space, '.' excludes \n \r U+2028 U+2029, [] / [^], \cX, \uXXXX incl. surrogate pairs, \u{...}, named groups and \k<..>, ']' / '}' / lone '{' / Python-only groups / possessive '+' / letter identity escapes / \p rejected as re.error -> exit 2 'bad pattern'), patterns pre-checked for both engines; adr breaker treats None vs text as a change ('INVARIANTS.md deleted (INV-A, INV-B)'); friction keys unsigned attempts by 'exit code N from <cmd>' and treats a missing log as zero attempts; --new requires a task id regex and membership in --tasks (exit 2, nothing written); --since rejects revs starting with '-', non-checkouts and unknown commits (exit 2). Note on finding 4: under the 'u' flag (JSON Schema's dialect per the official test suite) ^[]a]$ is a syntax error, not a non-match, so it is rejected loudly.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: The Edit/Write tools write \uXXXX escapes in their content literally
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: They decoded some of them: test data typed as "\u00a0", "\u2028", r"\u0042" and r"\uD83D\uDE00" landed in test_governance.py as raw NBSP / U+2028 characters, as 'B' and as the emoji, so three mutants of the \u handling survived for no good reason. The ECMA test data is now ASCII-only: patterns are written with '%' for the backslash (bs()) and special characters via chr(). Process note for successors, like gen-002's heredoc note: Bash heredocs halve backslashes, Edit/Write may decode \u.
